keepsake.name: Walking Stick Badge
keepsake.line: A little enamel badge for the walking stick, the sort that says you have been somewhere and made a point of it. Mum has hung it where the visitors cannot miss it.

keepsake.name: Tin of Kendal Mint Cake
keepsake.line: Kendal Mint Cake: nearly all sugar, and carried up Everest in 1953. Mum says it is the only sweet that counts as equipment.

keepsake.name: Well-Worn Boot
keepsake.line: One boot, resoled twice. It has been down every road in the League and has the opinions to prove it. Meadow has tried to sleep in it.

champions.title: Watcher of the Glaslyn nest
champions.reason: Bethan sits by the Glaslyn nest from the first egg to the last fledgling, and has views on anyone who coughs. She will fight you, but quietly.

champions.title: Cornish blood, Beara road
champions.reason: Jago's family came over from Cornwall for the copper at Allihies and simply never left. He is the only man on Beara who says "my lover" and "Slán" in the same breath.

champions.title: Under the Old Man of Storr
champions.reason: Calum has led walkers under the Old Man of Storr for years. He knows which way the Quiraing will move next, which is down, and says so cheerfully.

champions.title: Trains where Everest trained
champions.reason: Gareth trains on the slopes round Pen-y-Gwryd, where the 1953 Everest team did, and mentions it whether or not you asked.

champions.title: After the gwyniad
champions.reason: Elis fishes Llyn Tegid for the gwyniad, a whitefish found nowhere else in Wales, and has never once been seen to land one.

champions.title: Still checks the light
champions.reason: Aled used to keep a light on this coast, and still turns up at dusk to make sure the new arrangements are behaving.

champions.title: Walks to Thurles on match days
champions.reason: Seán walks the old road to Thurles on match days, and will tell you, unprompted, that the GAA was founded in the town in 1884.

champions.title: Plays between the sessions
champions.reason: Aoife plays the fiddle in Ennis, a town where it is hard to find a pub without a session, and walks this road between sets to rest her fingers.

champions.route: Hook Head and the Waterford Coast
champions.title: Talks about the light as if he lit it
champions.reason: Éamon shows visitors round Hook Lighthouse, one of the oldest working lighthouses in the world, and speaks of it as if he had lit it himself.

champions.title: The eel's life story
champions.reason: Brendan fishes the Lower Bann for eels, as his family always has. He says the eel's life is stranger than yours: it starts in the Sargasso Sea.

champions.title: More islands than he can count
champions.reason: Colm ferries folk across Lough Erne, which has more islands than he can be bothered to count, and has a story for every one of them.

champions.title: Up Pendle before breakfast
champions.reason: Gwen runs up Pendle Hill before work. The witches of 1612 are a story, she says; the hill is the real thing, and steeper than it looks.

champions.title: Guards a ruin, gladly
champions.reason: Hugh looks after Richmond Castle, which has stood over the Swale since the eleventh century, and says it has weathered the wait better than he has.

champions.title: Marches Ermine Street in full kit
champions.reason: Dai marches the line of Ermine Street in a full legionary's kit, because the road ran this way and nobody has stopped him.

champions.title: Has seen everyone try to climb it
champions.reason: Fiona looks after a stretch of the Wall and has seen every kind of person try to climb it. It was built to keep things out, she says, and now mostly keeps walkers in a line.

champions.title: Rides the marches
champions.reason: Joanne rides the marches every summer in the old way, and is the only person on the Debatable Land who knows exactly whose side she is on: her own.

champions.title: Missed the noise
champions.reason: Ken worked the foundry until it shut, and now walks the canals to see what is left of the noise. Quite a lot, he says, if you shout.

champions.title: Finds something every week
champions.reason: Rhiannon digs for a living and finds a new thing every week, and loses a trowel every other. She says the chalk gives with one hand and takes with the other.

champions.title: Walks where the trains used to run
champions.reason: Priscilla is a Cambridge don who walks the old Varsity Line, which once carried students between Oxford and Cambridge. The line closed in the sixties; the arguments about it have lasted longer than the trains did.

champions.title: Watches the Martello towers
champions.reason: Carol watches the coast from the shelter of a Martello tower, built against Napoleon, who never came. She says it has been very effective.

champions.title: End to end, more than once
champions.reason: Haf has walked Offa's Dyke from end to end more times than she'll admit. It is 177 miles, and she says the king would have been furious about the footpath.

champions.title: Coast to coast, on foot
champions.reason: Anne stalks deer on the hills the Southern Upland Way crosses, from one coast of Scotland to the other. She has never been seen by a deer, and says so often.

champions.title: Ninety-six miles, mostly in the rain
champions.reason: Eilidh guides walkers along the West Highland Way, 96 miles from Milngavie to Fort William. She says the midges are the real guides and she is only the interpreter.

champions.title: Missed the smelter
champions.reason: Dougie worked at the aluminium works in Kinlochleven until it closed, and says the water that powered it still sounds like overtime.

champions.title: Knows the hollow mountain
champions.reason: Ian looks after the trees above Loch Awe, in the shadow of Ben Cruachan, which has a power station hollowed out inside it. He thinks that's showing off.

champions.title: Rob Roy's biographer, in a way
champions.reason: Margaret is a historian of Rob Roy MacGregor, who was a cattle dealer, an outlaw and, by the end, a legend. She says the last paid best.

champions.title: Counts the cliff birds
champions.reason: Isobel counts seabirds on the Angus cliffs and has been sworn at by gannets. She says a fulmar will spit at you and then deny it.

champions.title: Still looking for the rest of the chessmen
champions.reason: Iain combs the sands at Uig, where the Lewis Chessmen were found in 1831. He says there are still a few pieces missing, and he intends to find them.

champions.title: Knits while she walks
champions.reason: Ina knits in the Shetland way and does it walking, which she says is just good time management. Every pattern is a family secret, and she will tell you three.

champions.title: Farms by the book town
champions.reason: Jock farms near Wigtown, Scotland's National Book Town, and says the only thing he reads is the sky.
